request.description: Design a housing for my board (3RL_WLC_PCB.zip).

product.name: JR Electro Kits 3-relay water level controller board (3RL_WLC) in a new two-piece housing
product.category: Pump / water level controller (relay board) with custom enclosure
product.summary: Most likely a three-relay automatic water level (pump) controller. The file name 3RL_WLC, three relays (K1, K3 large power type, K2 small), two 3-way input terminals feeding four DIP-4 optocouplers, a column of seven indicator LEDs and the jrelectrokits.com silkscreen all point that way. I am fairly confident of the function, less so of the controller chip (bottom side, not visible) and of the supply voltage (12 V assumed; a TO-220 regulator makes the logic rail). The housing is a new design: a tray base and a deep lid, 2 mm walls, split at terminal height so wire-entry notches need no side action, held by four M3 screws through the board's mounting holes. Scale comes from the stated 80 x 85 mm outline; the 5.08 mm terminal pitch in the picture agrees.
product.powerInput: 2-way screw terminal J1, assumed 12 V DC (possibly AC via bottom-side diodes), about 0.25 A

parts.name: Housing base (tray)
parts.function: Carries the board on four 5 mm bosses; front and rear walls have open-topped wire-entry notches (z -7.5 to -2) in front of J5, J7, J6 and behind J3, J2, J1.
parts.material: ABS or PC+ABS, UL94 V-0 (PETG or ASA for a printed prototype)
parts.process: Injection moulding, straight pull, 1 to 2 degree draft; or FDM print
parts.evidence: New design sized from the 80 x 85 mm board: 2 mm clearance each side, 2 mm walls, 5 mm under the board for solder tails and bottom SMD parts.
parts.unknowns: Wall-mount lugs or DIN clip not added; say if needed. Notch widths: 16 mm for 3-way and 11 mm for 2-way terminals, centred on each block.

parts.name: Housing lid (cover)
parts.function: Covers the relays and regulator with about 2.9 mm clearance, clamps the board with four posts, closes the tops of the wire notches, and has seven 3.2 mm holes for LED light pipes plus an optional 4 mm screwdriver hole over RV1.
parts.process: Injection moulding, straight pull; a lip and groove on the split line is recommended
parts.evidence: New design; height set by the tallest parts (power relays about 20.5 mm, upright TO-220 about 19 mm) plus clearance and a 2 mm roof.
parts.unknowns: Confirm relay height before fixing lid depth. Add vent slots only if the regulator runs hot.

parts.name: Base screw boss (moulded into base)
parts.function: Supports the board 5 mm above the floor at each mounting hole; has a 3.4 mm clearance hole and a counterbore underneath for the screw head.
parts.process: Moulded integral, with gussets to the wall
parts.evidence: One per 3.7 mm mounting hole at board (6,6), (74,6), (6,79), (74,79).

parts.name: Lid screw post (moulded into lid)
parts.function: Comes down to the top of the board at each mounting hole to clamp it and takes the thread-forming screw in a 2.5 mm pilot hole.
parts.process: Moulded integral, 1 degree draft, cored to avoid sink
parts.evidence: New design; checked clear of J1, J3, K1, K2 and the LEDs by position.

parts.name: M3 x 16 thread-forming screw
parts.function: Passes up through base boss and board hole into the lid post, holding base, board and lid together.
parts.package: Pan head, PT-type thread for plastics
parts.evidence: 3.7 mm mounting holes suit M3.

parts.name: LED light pipe
parts.function: Carries light from each upright 3 mm LED to the lid top face.
parts.process: Injection moulded, press-fit in lid (or one moulded comb of seven)
parts.evidence: The seven LEDs stand vertically about 5.5 mm tall while the lid roof is about 23 mm above the board, so they need pipes (or LEDs fitted on long leads).

parts.name: Main board 3RL_WLC
parts.function: Carries all the electronics: supply, controller, probe inputs, relay drivers and relays.
parts.process: Through-hole parts on top, SMD on the bottom
parts.evidence: Outline 80 x 85 x 1.6 mm, 2 copper layers, four 3.7 mm holes from the board data; green mask, silkscreen 'www.jrelectrokits.com', 'Made in India', 'TOP' in the picture.

parts.name: J1 supply input screw terminal, 2-way 5.08 mm
parts.function: Supply input to the board.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J1, two large pads at board (58.74, 80.87) and (63.82, 80.87); a track runs from it toward C1 and the regulator.
parts.unknowns: Supply voltage and polarity are not marked; trace the pads or check the kit instructions.

parts.name: J2 input screw terminal, 3-way 5.08 mm
parts.function: Probably level-probe or float-switch inputs for one tank (common plus two levels).
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J2, three pads at board y 80.62; sits directly above optocouplers U3 and U4.
parts.unknowns: Pin assignment unknown; trace to the optocoupler LED pins.

parts.name: J3 input screw terminal, 3-way 5.08 mm
parts.function: Probably level-probe or float-switch inputs for the second tank or sump.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J3, three pads at board y 80.62; sits above optocouplers U5 and U6.
parts.unknowns: Pin assignment unknown.

parts.name: J5 relay K1 output terminal, 2-way 5.08 mm
parts.function: Switched contact of K1 for the load (pump or contactor).
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J5; wide copper from K1 contact pads to both J5 pads is visible.

parts.name: J7 relay K3 output terminal, 2-way 5.08 mm
parts.function: Switched contact of K3 for the second load.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J7; wide copper from K3 contact pads to J7 is visible.

parts.name: J6 relay K2 output terminal, 3-way 5.08 mm
parts.function: Changeover contact of K2 (COM, NO, NC), for example an alarm or valve.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J6; three wide tracks run from K2's contact pads to the three J6 pads.

parts.name: K1 power relay (T90 / 30 A style footprint)
parts.function: Switches the main load on J5.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen K1 with coil and contact symbols; four 3 mm pads at board (15.81, 39.48), (6.91, 21.74), (6.91, 14.14), (24.71, 24.28) plus two coil pads; outline about 32 mm long.
parts.unknowns: Silkscreen outline is L-shaped and widens to 27.6 mm over the lower 13 mm; the real relay may be the full 27.5 mm wide. Measure the fitted relay (width, height) and its coil voltage.

parts.name: K3 power relay (same footprint as K1)
parts.function: Switches the second load on J7.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen K3, identical pad pattern 29.78 mm to the right of K1.
parts.unknowns: Same as K1.

parts.name: K2 small changeover relay (sugar-cube footprint)
parts.function: Changeover output on J6.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen K2; five pads with 12.2 mm coil-to-contact spacing and 12 mm row width, matching the common SRD-type 10 A relay.
parts.unknowns: Coil voltage; read the relay marking.

parts.name: U2 voltage regulator, TO-220 upright
parts.function: Makes the logic rail (assumed 5 V) from the supply.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen U2, three in-line pads at board x 71.2 with a 4.6 x 10.2 mm tabbed outline, next to electrolytics C1 and C2.
parts.unknowns: Output voltage; read the marking.

parts.name: C1 electrolytic capacitor, 10 mm
parts.function: Bulk capacitor on the incoming supply.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen C1, polarised 10 mm circle at board (74.2, 61.5), on the track from J1.
parts.unknowns: Value and height (a 1000 uF part may be 16 to 20 mm tall).

parts.name: C2 electrolytic capacitor, 10 mm
parts.function: Bulk capacitor on the regulator output (or second supply filter).
parts.evidence: Silkscreen C2, polarised 10 mm circle at board (64.9, 56.4) beside U2.
parts.unknowns: Value and which rail it sits on.

parts.name: U3 to U6 optocouplers, DIP-4
parts.function: Isolate the four level-probe or float inputs from the controller.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen U3, U4, U5, U6 with notch marks; four pads each on a 2.54 x 7.62 mm grid; placed between the input terminals and the controller area.
parts.unknowns: They could also be opto-triacs or other DIP-4 parts; read the marking.

parts.name: Q1, Q3, Q2 relay driver transistors
parts.function: Low-side switches for the three relay coils.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen Q1 beside K1, Q3 beside K3, Q2 above K2; three in-line pads each.
parts.unknowns: Package and type; the 3.5 x 8.2 mm outline fits either.

parts.name: RV1 trimmer potentiometer
parts.function: Set-once adjustment, probably probe sensitivity or a delay time.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen RV1, about 9.8 mm square outline with three pads in a triangle at board (50.6, 54.9).
parts.unknowns: Value and what it sets; trace the wiper.

parts.name: J8 pin header, 1 x 6
parts.function: Probably the programming or serial header for the controller.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J8, six in-line pads at board x 57.7, y 52 to 64.7, pin 1 marked.
parts.unknowns: Could instead take a 6-pin module (serial or radio); no housing opening provided. Say if it must be reachable.

parts.name: J4 pin header, 1 x 4
parts.function: Auxiliary header, possibly serial, I2C or an external sensor or buzzer.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen J4, four in-line pads at board x 20.4, y 52.2 to 59.8.
parts.unknowns: Function unknown; if a cable leaves the box from here, a notch is needed.

parts.name: D16, D15, D14, D13, D11, D9, D8 indicator LEDs, 3 mm
parts.function: Status column: probably power, tank levels and relay or pump states.
parts.evidence: Silkscreen D16 to D8 with round flat-sided outlines, two pads each at board x 1.9 and 4.4, down the left edge.
parts.unknowns: Colours and meaning of each LED; needed for lid legends.

parts.name: Controller IC with support passives (bottom side)
parts.function: Reads the isolated level inputs and RV1, drives the LEDs and the three relay transistors.
parts.evidence: Bottom-side pad group P1: 54 pads in 21.1 x 15.6 mm at board (35.5, 55.63), under the dense via field; 54 pads fits a 28-pin SMD IC plus about 13 passives.
parts.unknowns: Not visible in the top picture. Photograph the bottom and read the marking; it could even be discrete logic.

parts.name: Supply input diodes (bottom side, SMA-size)
parts.function: Probably reverse-polarity protection or a bridge rectifier on the J1 input.
parts.evidence: Bottom-side two-pad groups P9, P10, P11 (3.5 x 5.6 mm) and P24 (4.4 x 3.55 mm) clustered under J1.
parts.unknowns: These could be large capacitors or resistors instead; inspect the bottom side.

parts.name: Left-edge SMD resistors (bottom side)
parts.function: Probably series resistors for the LED column.
parts.evidence: Bottom-side two-pad groups P28 to P32 at board x 1.75, pitched 6.68 mm like the LEDs above them.
parts.unknowns: Values; they sit 1.75 mm from the board edge, so keep base ribs away from that strip.

parts.name: Other bottom-side SMD passive clusters
parts.function: Pull-ups, base resistors, decoupling capacitors and probably relay flyback diodes.
parts.evidence: Bottom-side groups P2, P6, P7, P8, P16, P25, P27, P87, P90, P3 in the board data.
parts.unknowns: Each position is a cluster, not one part; the true passive count is higher (277 pad groups in total, many of them vias).

connections.evidence: Typical 0.9 W coil for this relay size.

connections.evidence: Controller plus LEDs and opto pull-ups fed from this rail.

connections.evidence: Tracks run from the optocoupler lower pins into the via field over the controller.

connections.evidence: RV1 sits in the controller area.

connections.evidence: Fan of parallel tracks from the controller area to the LED column.

connections.evidence: One transistor per relay.

connections.evidence: Q1 is beside K1's coil pads.

connections.evidence: Q3 is beside K3.

connections.evidence: Q2 is directly above K2.

connections.label: K1 switched contact (external circuit)
connections.evidence: Wide copper visible from K1 contacts to J5. Voltage is the user's load circuit, assumed mains; current limited by the 5.08 mm terminals and track width, not the relay.

connections.evidence: Wide copper visible from K3 contacts to J7; same limits as K1.

connections.evidence: Three wide tracks visible from K2 to J6; current limited by the relay class and tracks.

connections.label: Programming / serial header
connections.evidence: A 1 x 6 header near a controller is typical for programming.

connections.evidence: Function not determinable from the picture.

connections.evidence: Housing design.

connections.evidence: Housing design.

connections.evidence: Housing design.

controls.label: Trimmer RV1 (set-point)
controls.action: Turning it with a screwdriver changes a set-point, probably probe sensitivity or a pump delay; the exact function is not known from the data.

unknowns: Controller type and all bottom-side parts: only pad groups are known. A photo of the populated bottom side would settle them.
Supply voltage at J1 (12 V DC assumed) and relay coil voltages. Read the relay markings and the U2 marking.
Real relay body size for K1 and K3: the silkscreen is L-shaped, and a full-width 27.5 mm relay would come close to LEDs D8 and D9 and to Q1. Relay height sets the lid depth.
Exact meaning of J2 and J3 pins and of each LED; needed for lid legends.
Whether J4 or J8 must be reachable from outside; no opening is provided for them.
Heights of C1, C2 and U2 are estimated from the package; the lid allows up to about 23 mm above the board.
Component positions for parts not in the pad list (K2, C1, C2, Q1 to Q3, U3 to U6, LEDs, headers) were scaled from the picture at about 18.8 px per mm; expect up to 0.5 mm error.
With the lid off, the board only rests on the base bosses (the screws clamp it through to the lid). Add two snap hooks or separate board screws if wiring with the board fixed is wanted.
verifySteps: Measure the height of the tallest fitted part (relays, U2, C1) above the board; the lid needs that plus at least 1.5 mm.
Photograph the bottom side and read the controller, diode and transistor markings.
Read the relay coil voltage and the U2 marking to confirm the 12 V in, 5 V logic assumption.
Check the K1 and K3 body width against the LED column and Q1.
Print the base and lid in PETG, fit the board, and check that each wire notch lines up with its terminal entry and each light pipe with its LED.
Trace J2 and J3 pins to the optocouplers, and J4 and J8 to the controller, to confirm their function.
Measure the supply current with all three relays on to confirm about 0.25 A.
safety: The relay contacts and J5, J6, J7 are likely to carry mains. Isolate the supply before opening the housing; the lid must need a tool to remove (it does, four screws).
Use a flame-retardant housing material (UL94 V-0) and keep the wire notches small enough that fingers cannot reach the terminals; add cable glands or strain relief for mains cables.
Keep at least 6 mm creepage between the relay contact side and the low-voltage side; do not add metal parts or screws in the contact area at the front of the board.
The 5.08 mm terminals and board tracks limit the load current to about 10 A even if the relays are rated higher. Use an external contactor for large pumps and an external fuse or breaker.
Level probes in water must stay on the isolated low-voltage side; do not share their wiring with mains conductors.
The linear regulator and relay coils warm the sealed box slightly (about 3 W at most); avoid mounting in direct sun, or add vents if not in a wet location.
